title: Advanced Diploma in Game Ranch Management

lessons.title: Managing a game ranch as a business and ecosystem
lessons.html:
The game ranch manager

The Advanced Diploma in Game Ranch Management (NQF 7) is aimed at middle managers in game ranching and natural resource management. South Africa has one of the largest private wildlife industries in the world, with income from live game sales, hunting, venison, eco-tourism and conservation projects. Managers must balance ecology, economics, people and law.

Ecological management

  • Veld condition assessment: regular surveys of grass species composition, basal cover and woody plant density. Increaser and decreaser grass species indicate whether veld is improving or degrading.
  • Carrying capacity: estimate how many grazers and browsers the ranch can support, expressed in large stock units or browser units, and adjust for rainfall. Overstocking in drought leads to die-offs and long-term damage.
  • Species mix: balance bulk grazers (buffalo, zebra, wildebeest), selective grazers (sable, roan), mixed feeders (impala, eland) and browsers (kudu, giraffe).
  • Fire management: planned burning to remove moribund grass and control bush, using firebreaks and a burning plan; neighbours must be informed, and fire protection associations involved.
  • Bush encroachment and alien plant control under the Conservation of Agricultural Resources Act 43 of 1983.
  • Water provision: placement of artificial waterpoints affects grazing pressure across the ranch.

Game counts and offtake

Annual aerial or road-strip counts give population estimates. From these, the manager sets a sustainable offtake quota for hunting, live sales and culling, based on growth rates, sex ratios and veld condition.

lessons.title: Finance, people, law and strategy
lessons.html:
The business side

Game ranching can be profitable, but costs are high: fencing, water, security, staff and veterinary work. Managers must prepare budgets, track income by enterprise and decide which mix of activities makes sense.

EnterpriseConsiderations
Live game salesMarket prices can rise and fall sharply; capture costs and permits
Trophy and biltong huntingSeasonal, needs professional hunters, outfitters and accommodation
VenisonNeeds registered game abattoir or harvesting under Meat Safety Act rules and a cold chain
Eco-tourismLodges, guiding, marketing, guest safety
Conservation partnershipsBiodiversity stewardship, carbon or research income

Legal compliance

  • Provincial conservation legislation: exemption or registration of properties, hunting permits, game transport permits.
  • National Environmental Management: Biodiversity Act 10 of 2004 and the Threatened or Protected Species (TOPS) regulations for listed species such as rhino, cheetah and sable in some cases.
  • Animal Diseases Act 35 of 1984: buffalo and other species are linked to diseases such as foot-and-mouth disease and corridor disease, and movement is controlled.
  • Firearms Control Act 60 of 2000 for staff using rifles.
  • Labour law and the OHS Act 85 of 1993 for staff.

People management and security

Rangers, field staff, lodge staff and anti-poaching teams must be recruited, trained and managed fairly. Poaching of rhino and bushmeat snaring are serious threats; managers work with security companies, SAPS and neighbours, and must ensure staff safety and lawful use of force.

Strategy

A strategic plan sets the ranch's long-term vision, for example moving from live sales towards a mixed hunting and tourism model. It includes risk management for drought, disease outbreaks, market shocks and fire.

Key points

  • Game ranch management balances ecology, economics, people and law.
  • Veld condition, carrying capacity and game counts guide stocking and offtake.
  • Income may come from live sales, hunting, venison, eco-tourism and conservation.
  • Comply with provincial permits, TOPS, disease control, firearm and labour laws.
  • Plan strategically and manage risks from drought, disease, markets, fire and poaching.

quiz.question: What is carrying capacity on a game ranch?

options.text: How many grazers and browsers the ranch can support
The size of a capture truck
The number of guests a lodge can host

quiz.question: Which animals are examples of browsers?
What is the purpose of annual game counts?

options.text: To estimate populations and set sustainable offtake

quiz.question: Which regulations protect listed species such as rhino?

options.text: TOPS regulations under the Biodiversity Act

quiz.question: Which law covers alien plant control and bush encroachment?

options.text: Conservation of Agricultural Resources Act 43 of 1983
